definitions.explanation: A machine that converts electrical energy into mechanical motion. Used broadly for electric motors in appliances, vehicles, and industrial equipment.

examples.japanese: モーター⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{回|まわ}っている→回る：01150_mawaru⟧。
モーター⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{音|おと}→音：00743_oto⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦うるさい→うるさい：00763_urusai⟧。
⟦{電気|でんき}→電気：09780_denki⟧モーター⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{動|うご}く→動く：00904_ugoku⟧⟦{自動車|じどうしゃ}→自動車：02886_jidousha⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{増|ふ}えている→増える：01183_fueru⟧。
examples.english: Cars powered by electric motors are increasing.

notes:
A loanword from English "motor." In Japanese, モーター typically refers to electric motors specifically, while ⟦エンジン→エンジン：03835_enjin⟧ is used for internal combustion engines. This distinction differs from English where "motor" can refer to either.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{電気|でんき}→電気：09780_denki⟧モーター: electric motor
- モーター⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{回|まわ}る→回る：01150_mawaru⟧: the motor runs/spins
- モーター⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{止|と}まる→止まる：00555_tomaru⟧: the motor stops
- モーター{音|おん}: motor noise

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦エンジン→エンジン：03835_enjin⟧: engine — typically for internal combustion engines (gasoline, diesel)
- {発動機|はつどうき}: engine, motor — a more technical Japanese term, less common in everyday speech
- ⟦{動力|どうりょく}→動力：18784_douryoku⟧: motive power — the abstract concept of power that drives machinery
